candidate_payload.research_markdown:
# Prevention-system completion research

The current system has strong components but does not satisfy the complete prevention property system-wide. The registry has 25 rows. None is proven to have one executable owner spanning classification, selection, activation, execution, correction, gates, resume, and terminal emission. The representative research controller is closest: it has a closed operation dispatcher, durable PREPARED/COMMITTED journals, exact role schemas, partial round admission, internal failed-fingerprint prevention, and mechanical timing.

Typed coverage is local rather than universal. Closed contracts exist for 13 operation kinds, 16 ledger event types, and 11 research-driver operations, while governed work still crosses Markdown commands, argparse strings, caller-built JSON, arbitrary argv, shell strings, and direct subprocess boundaries.

sequence_guard and sequence_checked_exec fail closed only when explicitly invoked. Official Codex PreToolUse supports Bash, apply_patch, and MCP, but is documented as incomplete for richer shell and other non-shell/non-MCP paths. Browser, subagent, and remote-workflow action classes therefore lack an evidenced authoritative interceptor.

Correction evidence is durable and fingerprint selection can route to a verified registered successor, but selection is optional and no universal action boundary prohibits replay. Observation can propose or link candidates, and an explicit lifecycle can qualify, promote, verify, and later reuse them; the end-to-end test proves this path but also proves that lifecycle invocation and approval remain separate.

Research round admission reserves five attempts and three role windows, but omits retry, package materialization, and terminal overhead. Resume mechanisms exist in the research driver, promotion journal, work-memory ledger, and workflow state store, but no common effect-identity contract covers every operational side effect. Metrics omit system-wide raw dispatch, recurring-action denominator, registered reuse, prevented failure, mechanical-failure time, and representative overhead.

Registry inventory: local-workflow-orch-image, greenfield-full-drive, remote-mcp-user-onboarding, taggable-source-reload, mawf-playbook-full-test, mawf-playbook-speed-test, mawf-playbook-blocker-reentry, github-app-repos-refresh, claude-auth-token-refresh, taggable-api-deploy, taggable-admin-spa-deploy, taggable-media-worker-deploy, airgapped-local-bulgarian-stt, airgapped-redaction-stack, callcenter-harness-provision-verify, airgapped-llm-judge, secure-landing-seed, callcenter-harness-engine-invariants, discovery-promotion-lifecycle, commit-push-main, discovery-bootstrap, discovery-candidate-reconciliation, convergence-checkpoint-run, scoped-context-edit, convergence-state-review-cycle. The finite evidence proves declared boundaries but excludes most external automation implementations, so hidden internal ownership cannot be credited; each row remains unproven until a common contract and black-box acceptance suite prove it.

exclusions: implementation planning or code changes during research
commit, push, deployment, secret access, external messaging, or phase-ledger contract changes
conversation transcripts, hidden reasoning, personal data, credentials, or raw terminal output as durable learning evidence
dashboard or user-interface design beyond the metric contracts required for acceptance
sequence catalog cleanup unrelated to the prevention-system acceptance requirements
in_scope: memory-knowledge operational sequence registry, selector, guard, checked execution, observer, blocker/correction ledger, discovery, promotion, registered verification, budget, resume, and metrics contracts
research-playbook execution only as one representative sequence and integration surface, not as the whole system
mcp-agents-workflow and Codex action boundaries only where required to ground automatic pre-action interception
official OpenAI Codex hook documentation only to establish the supported and unsupported pre-action interception boundary
all eight user-provided enforcement properties and all six user-provided measurable completion conditions
charter.objective: Assess the real current implementation against the complete mechanical-error prevention system and produce a planner-ready package that grounds every missing mechanism and end-to-end acceptance boundary without narrowing the goal.
research_questions: Does every operational sequence have one executable owner for initialization through terminal emission?
Are mechanical operations typed and schema-validated rather than reconstructed through shell, JSON, or text manipulation?
Can an authoritative host boundary intercept every mechanical action class before execution, including the action classes that official Codex hooks do and do not support?
Does a same-path-verified correction prohibit the failed fingerprint and become the mandatory successor?
Is intent through promoted registered reuse one automatically joined causal learning lifecycle?
Does admission reserve the entire atomic unit before long work begins?
Can every completed transition resume idempotently from durable state?
Do system-wide metrics prove registered reuse, prevented failures, recurrence reduction, and mechanical-overhead targets?
charter.supplied_input: The complete prevention system has one executable sequence owner, typed operations, automatic pre-action interception, mandatory verified correction replacement, automatic causal discovery-to-promotion learning, full-unit budget admission, durable idempotent resume, and system-wide enforcement metrics. Completion requires zero raw JSON/text patching in governed runs, zero repeated mechanical fingerprints, no under-budget long-stage start, mandatory reuse of verified corrections, at least 95 percent registered use for recurring actions, and mechanical overhead below 5 to 10 percent.
terminal_rules: PASS requires all three lenses to pass the same candidate and envelope hashes, a fresh adjudicator with no research-actionable finding, every planner obligation READY, exact package validation, and zero active agent slots.
GAPS means research-stage corrections remain inside this frozen charter.
BLOCKED means required accessible evidence or a named approval route is unavailable.
CAP_REACHED means the shared time, round, attempt, retry, or repeated-fingerprint cap fired.
